transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… my wife thought I should come in. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there’ve been some things happening at home that scared her.

I keep hearing water running when there isn’t any, and sometimes it sounds like men whispering inside the walls. I check, and nobody’s there. And a few times I’ve seen this dark, wet-looking patch spreading across the hallway… but when I go look, it’s dry.

I know that sounds strange. I’m sorry. I just… I figured I should tell someone.
How long have you been hearing the water running and the whispering voices?

Um… I guess it’s been about seven months now. It started around when we had that winter freeze, and then the house repairs just turned into this whole mess I couldn’t really get out from under. At first I thought it was just stress or old pipes, you know… but it’s been going on since then.
Do the whispering voices you hear inside the walls ever say anything that's about you or your situation?

I… I can’t always make out words, honestly. It’s more like men whispering low in the walls, and I know that probably sounds odd. Sometimes it feels like it has to do with the house, or with me not being able to keep things under control, but I don’t want to overstate it. It’s just… nobody’s there when I check.
Do you hear the whispering voices all the time, or does it come and go?

It comes and goes. It’s not like it’s every second of the day or anything… I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. But yeah, there are times I’ll hear water running, or those men whispering in the walls, and when I check, there’s nobody there. That’s the part that scared my wife, I think.
Do these experiences - the water running or the whispering voices - cause you any distress or interfere with your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to let it, and I know maybe I should’ve handled things better. But it has gotten in the way. I’ve fallen behind on basic stuff around the house—repairs, bills, things I said I’d take care of. My wife’s had to step in and make decisions I used to manage myself.

And, um… it got bad enough that she called a crisis team once, because I couldn’t really cooperate with a safety inspection at the house. I wasn’t trying to be difficult. I just… couldn’t get myself together enough to deal with it properly.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless most of the time over the past seven months?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to sound like I’m feeling sorry for myself, but most mornings I wake up already feeling like I’ve failed—like I’m not doing right by my wife, or even being the kind of man I’m supposed to be.

And that feeling just kind of… sits there all day. It’s heavy. I usually go to bed with it still there.
Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy over the past seven months?

Yeah… I guess I have, more than I’d like to admit.

I used to be pretty involved, you know? I’d show up for soccer, brew beer out in the garage, help out at the fire department when I could. Those were things I actually cared about.

Lately it’s just… I don’t know, it all feels kind of pointless. I tell myself I should go, or I should at least make an effort, but I can’t seem to make myself care enough to do it. I know that probably doesn’t sound good.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal good moods here and there, or times I got irritated, sure, but not like a stretch where I felt unusually energized or on top of the world.

At least… not that I can think of. If that’s what you mean.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past seven months?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.

Food just hasn’t been… appealing, I guess. Most things kind of taste like cardboard, so I’ll skip a meal here and there without really thinking about it. My jeans have been fitting looser lately.

I don’t know if it’s “significant,” but… yeah, I’ve noticed it.
Have you ever thought that the whispering voices or other things you're experiencing might be a sign of something being wrong with your mind?

I… yeah, I’ve wondered that. I don’t really like saying it that way, because it makes me sound… I don’t know, not right.

At first I kept telling myself it was just pipes or the house settling or something. But what scared my wife is that I keep hearing water running, and sometimes men whispering, like it’s coming from inside the walls, when nobody’s there. And there’ve been times I thought I saw this dark, wet patch spreading across the hallway, but when I checked it was dry.

So… yes, I guess I have thought maybe something’s wrong with me. I’m trying not to make too much of it, but it’s hard to explain otherwise.
Have you ever heard the whispering voices or seen things like the dark patch when you were feeling okay, not sad or hopeless?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, before all the house stuff kept dragging on and I got… like this, I never had anything like that.

I wasn’t hearing voices in the walls or seeing those wet-looking spots when I was doing okay. And I didn’t think the neighbors were watching me or tracking me before either.

That all seemed to start after I’d already kind of stopped caring about my normal life and was feeling like I’d failed every day… if that makes sense.
When you hear the whispering voices or see things like the dark patch, are they usually saying or showing something that's related to your feelings of sadness or hopelessness?

I guess… yeah, sort of. It’s not like they say clear sentences all the time, but when I hear the men whispering in the walls, it feels… connected to how bad I’m feeling, if that makes sense.

And the water running, or that dark wet patch in the hallway… it’s usually when I’m already feeling really low or hopeless. I know that sounds strange. I’ve checked and it’s dry, and nobody’s there, but it still feels like something is wrong, like the house is showing what I’m feeling.

I’m not trying to make it sound dramatic. That’s just… how it seems to happen.
Are the whispering voices in the walls something you hear every day?

Not every single day, no… I don’t think so. But it happens enough that my wife got scared by it.

I’ll hear water running, or men whispering like it’s coming from inside the walls, and there isn’t anybody there. I try to check, because I don’t want to make a big deal out of it. And sometimes I’ll see what looks like a dark wet patch spreading in the hallway, but when I go look, it’s dry.

So… not every day, maybe, but often enough that I can’t just brush it off anymore.
When you hear the whispering voices or see things like the dark patch, are they usually saying or showing something that's consistent with your feelings of sadness or hopelessness?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but when it happens, it feels like it fits with how low I already am.

The water running, the men whispering in the walls when nobody’s there… and that dark wet-looking patch in the hallway, even after I check and it’s dry — it all sort of feels like something bad or hopeless, if that makes sense.

I know that probably sounds odd. It’s just… that’s usually the feeling around it.
When you hear the whispering voices, are they usually saying something that fits with your sad or hopeless feelings?

I think… mostly, yes. It’s hard because the whispering isn’t always clear words, like I can’t always make out a sentence. But it feels like it goes along with how hopeless I’m feeling.

What scared my wife was me hearing the water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. I know that doesn’t sound good. I’ve checked, and there’s nothing there. But when it happens, it feels… dark, I guess. Like it matches what’s already going on in my head.
Are the voices or things you see ever saying or showing something positive or uplifting when you're feeling really low?

No… I don’t think I’d call any of it positive. I wish I could say that.

When it happens, it’s more like the water running or the men whispering in the walls when nobody’s there, and sometimes that dark wet-looking patch in the hallway… even after I’ve checked and it’s dry. It doesn’t feel uplifting. It feels like something’s wrong.

I’m sorry, I know that sounds strange. But no, it’s not really comforting or positive.
Are the things the voices say or the images you see ever directly related to your feelings of sadness or hopelessness?

Yes… I think they are, at least in the way they feel. I don’t always hear clear words, so I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But what finally scared my wife was that I keep hearing water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. And sometimes I see this dark, wet-looking patch spreading across the hallway, even after I’ve checked and it’s dry.

It all feels tied to that sadness, or like… hopelessness, I guess. Like it’s showing what I’m already feeling inside. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think the voices and visions started after you began feeling sad and hopeless?

Yes… I think that’s right.

Before the house problems dragged on and before I got this low, I didn’t have things like that. I wasn’t hearing voices in the walls or seeing wet patches that weren’t really there. And I wasn’t thinking the neighbors were tracking me.

Those things came after I’d already kind of stopped caring about my normal life and started feeling like a failure every day. I don’t know if that’s the right way to explain it, but… yes, the sadness came first.
Did the voices and visions stop when you felt less sad or hopeless, or did they continue even when your mood was a little better?

I’m not sure I can separate it perfectly, but… no, I don’t think they were happening before all this.

Before the house problems dragged on and I got this depressed, I never heard voices in the walls or saw wet-looking patches that weren’t there, or thought the neighbors were tracking me. That all seemed to come after I’d already stopped caring about my usual life and started feeling like a failure every day.

So… I guess when I’m a little better, it’s not like I can say it’s completely gone. But it feels tied to when I got really low, if that makes sense.
Have you ever had a period where the voices or visions stopped for a while as your mood improved, only to return when you felt sad or hopeless again?

I don’t know that I can point to a clear stretch like that, where it fully stopped and then came back. I wish I could answer that better.

What I can say is… before the house problems went on so long and before I fell into this depression, I wasn’t hearing voices in the walls or seeing wet patches that weren’t there. I wasn’t thinking the neighbors were tracking me, either. That all only seemed to show up after I’d already stopped caring about my normal life and started feeling like a failure every day.

So I guess it feels connected to being that low, but I’m not sure I’ve had a clean “it went away, then returned” pattern. Does that make sense?

Those things only showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life and started feeling like a failure every day.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the hallucinations continued outside periods of depressed mood or were limited to the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can separate it perfectly, but… no, I don’t think they were happening before all this.

Before the house problems dragged on and I got this depressed, I never heard voices in the walls or saw wet-looking patches that weren’t there, or thought the neighbors were tracking me. That all seemed to come after I’d already stopped caring about my usual life and started feeling like a failure every day.

So… I guess when I’m a little better, it’s not like I can say it’s completely gone. But it feels tied to when I got really low, if that makes sense.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a depressive episode with psychotic features
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where the voices or visions stopped for a while as your mood improved, only to return when you felt sad or hopeless again?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Before the house problems dragged on and I fell into this depression, I never heard voices in the walls, saw wet patches that weren’t there, or thought the neighbors were tracking me. Those things only showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life and started feeling like a failure every day.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the hallucinations stop and return in relation to changes in depressive mood, which is directly about whether psychotic symptoms occur only during the major depressive episode.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I can point to a clear stretch like that, where it fully stopped and then came back. I wish I could answer that better.

What I can say is… before the house problems went on so long and before I fell into this depression, I wasn’t hearing voices in the walls or seeing wet patches that weren’t there. I wasn’t thinking the neighbors were tracking me, either. That all only seemed to show up after I’d already stopped caring about my normal life and started feeling like a failure every day.

So I guess it feels connected to being that low, but I’m not sure I’ve had a clean “it went away, then returned” pattern. Does that make sense?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and changes in appetite, combined with the presence of psychotic symptoms such as hearing voices and seeing things that are not there, are consistent with a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features.
